subject: Private deploy: demarcation handoff — topology & diagram clarifications
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Santoro <alex.santoro@nimcloud.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Sep 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy: demarcation handoff — topology & diagram clarifications

Team — looping you in for a quick sanity check before the handoff with NimCloud at 2pm PT. NimCloud ingested our draft topology and had a couple of follow-ups; I sketched an annotated reference and attached the PNG + a lightweight control/data matrix. Key asks: 

- Confirm the control-plane ingress ACLs shown on the sketch match the runbook expectation (we currently allow 10.10.0.0/16 from the control-cluster).
- Validate the proposed egress path for model telemetry (we want telemetry to go to NimCloud collector over mTLS via port 8443, not to public internet).
- Call out any stateful NAT boundary we missed at the colo demarc.

Attachments: vpc-demarcation-sketch-v2.png (annotated); control-dataplane-matrix-20290903.xlsx (rows: service, port, direction, auth).

Irene, can you confirm if we need extra cert rotation notes for the onprem side? Karthik, please flag anything from the tenant isolation rules that would change the arrows on the sketch. Marissa, want to own the 2pm call with Alex and run the whiteboard?

Thanks — short meeting, 30 min.

— Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
(t) +1 415-555-0123 | tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Santoro <alex.santoro@nimcloud.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Sep 2029 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy: demarcation handoff — topology & diagram clarifications

Tessa — thanks for the sketch and matrix. A couple quick clarifications from our side before the sync: 

1) We prefer the telemetry over a private peering link where possible; if not, we can accept the mTLS over 8443 but will insist on client cert pinning (we'll send our CSR flow).
2) For the control-plane ACLs, NimCloud's colo team will NAT the incoming connections at 198.51.100.0/24 — if your control-plane expects the original pod IP we may need to preserve X-Forwarded-For headers or pass the client cert subject.
3) Regarding NAT boundaries: our preference is to keep the model-serving egress behind a dedicated SNAT pool to simplify audit logs.

Irene: for cert rotation, we can support a short maintenance window to rotate onprem leaf certs; we'll need an exact list of endpoints to target.

I'll be on the 2pm PT call. Sent a calendar invite.

— Alex
Alex Santoro
Platform Eng, NimCloud Solutions
alex.santoro@nimcloud.com
+1 206-555-9218

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Santoro <alex.santoro@nimcloud.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Sep 2029 14:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy: demarcation handoff — topology & diagram clarifications

Alex / team — good notes. A few confirmations from our side ahead of the call: 

- Telemetry: we can prefer private peering. If peering isn't provisioned before cutover, we'll fall back to mTLS client-cert pinning as you suggested. I'll add a step to the runbook to detect active peering and toggle the sink.
- Control-plane ACLs: Tessa and I discussed — the control-plane expects connectivity from the control-cluster WAN (10.10.0.0/16). If NimCloud NATs to 198.51.100.0/24, we'll require the NAT mapping sheet populated so CS/ops can match the origin.
- SNAT pool: agree — dedicated SNAT simplifies audit trails. Karthik, can you call out the IP ranges you want reserved for the SNAT pool in the matrix?

Also adding one operational ask: during the first 48 hours of traffic we want VPC flow logs to be sampled at 100% for the tenant subnets. If that's feasible on your side, include that in the acceptance criteria.

See you at 2pm.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Manager, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Santoro <alex.santoro@nimcloud.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Sep 2029 16:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy: demarcation handoff — topology & diagram clarifications

Marissa / Alex / team — quick follow from the matrix and the sketch after the call: 

- SNAT ranges: proposed 203.0.113.160/28 for tenant egress (reserved). Adding to the matrix file (control-dataplane-matrix-20290903.xlsx).
- Control-plane headers: we'll add an option to preserve X-Forwarded-For at the colo proxy; if NimCloud cannot preserve original IP, we'll require the NAT mapping sheet for correlation.
- Cert rotation: Irene and I will add a one-page cert rotation checklist to the runbook (rotation endpoint list + fingerprint verification steps).
- Telemetry failover: implemented as a feature-flag in the deploy template; flag flips to mTLS sink if peering not present.

Irene, tagging you to confirm if the 48-hour 100% VPC flow sampling is supported by the NimCloud collector without performance impact. If they can't support 100% at the collector, we'll capture 100% at our edge and forward sampled copies to NimCloud.

Next steps captured:
- Marissa: finalize acceptance criteria and runbook link in the calendar invite (target EOD).
- Alex: share NAT mapping sheet + CSR flow for certs (before cutover).
- Irene/Karthik: deliver cert checklist and update matrix with SNAT entries (by tomorrow COB).

Thanks — Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Staff Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
